fix: Make locate allocation-free on every pointer move: it currently calls self.ordered(list) (live_items() clones the whole items Vec, filters, collects and sorts) and then collects `others` and a `Vec<Rect>` for flow_of (reorder.rs:616-624). Count/iterate the lists and items directly, or cache per-list ordered rects behind a generation counter bumped on rect/list/item changes, so drag_update allocates nothing in steady state.

Clone the Session (which clones K) only after the drop slot is known to have changed. Locate on a borrow first: `let guard = core.session.borrow(); let Some(current) = guard.as_ref() else { return }; let (list, to) = core.locate(current); if (list, to) == (current.to_list, current.to) { return; } drop(guard);` then clone and mutate as before. locate does not borrow core.session, so the borrow is safe. Most pointer moves hit the early return, so they then clone nothing.

auto_scroll runs on every drag_update and on every scheduled frame while near an edge, but only needs session.pointer. Replace the Session clone with a copy of the pointer: `let (Some(pointer), Some(geometry)) = (core.session.borrow().as_ref().map(|session| session.pointer), node.geometry.get()) else { return; };` and use `pointer.y` in place of `session.pointer.y` at lines 883-884.

The keyboard path clones the whole Session (and K) on every arrow press, including presses that hit the list boundary and return at line 955. Check the target index through a borrow first (`let to = core.session.borrow().as_ref().map(|s| s.to as isize + step);`), return on out-of-range, and clone only for an in-range move that is then written back at line 959.

ordered() builds, sorts and returns a Vec of every item in the list just to take its length. Add `fn count(&self, list: usize) -> usize` on Core that counts live items with rects in that list (keeping the retain of dead items that live_items does) and use it here. The same pattern appears at line 972 (nudge_by) and line 831 (finish), so change those too.

bind runs on every build for every reorder item and always clones the key, even when unchanged. Use `item.key.borrow_mut().clone_from(&self.key);`, which reuses the existing storage for owned keys (same pattern already used for the label at line 1030).

The label is cloned only to read it into format!. Borrow instead: `let label = item.label.borrow(); let label = label.as_deref().unwrap_or("Item");` (scope the guard so it drops before request_rebuild). Apply the same change to the identical clone in nudge_by at lines 977-981, which runs per screen-reader action.
